messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: Rstudio & .stan files: prevent soft-wrap?
parts: Probably a query more appropriately directed to the rstudio folks, but just in case anyone on this list has encountered and solve this already: is there any way to get rstudio to *not* soft-wrap .stan files? Love the proper code highlighting for .stan files in rstudio, but I'm a glutton for long comment lines and prefer unwrapped views.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Rstudio & .stan files: prevent soft-wrap?
parts:
We (and Google code style, which we're primarily following),
strongly recommend a max of 80-character lines. The main reason
for us is that diff tools like the ones in GitHub are line
based and when you try to view online with something like
GitHub file viewers, it's a huge pain if the lines are wider
than that. Given that Stan looks a lot like C++ when written,
we recommend pretty much following this:

http://google.github.io/styleguide/cppguide.html

for exactly the reasons they lay out.

So rather than writing:

a <- b; // a really really long comment that's going to run over

we'd suggest

// a really really long
// comment that can now be wrapped
// and won't run over
a <- b;

And even more strongly we'd suggest renaming variables or writing
functions with meaningful names so you don't need long in-code comments.
The big problem is that (a) comments get stale, whereas code never
lies, and (b) it's hard to read the code when there are a lot of comments
and you always need to read the code because of (a).

If you have long program comments about things like algorithms or
references, we suggest putting them up top in a /* ... */ comment.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Rstudio & .stan files: prevent soft-wrap?
parts:
On Wednesday, August 5, 2015 at 1:02:00 PM UTC-4, Jeffrey Arnold wrote:
Probably not. Rstudio is still an R-focused IDE, so, while it supports some other filetypes, it doesn't have as many editor features for them.

RStudio seems not to soft-wrap C++ source, so the OP could ask RStudio about treating a .stan file like a .cpp file unless subsumed by Stan logic.

Ben

Yeah, I've known for a while I *should* be respecting the margins, especially for comments; I'll endeavor to make the switch now :O)

That said, I ended up "solving" this self-made problem by using the sublime-stan syntax package (previously mentioned here; https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/stan-users/xZqQM3qsLps) for sublime text, my preferred editor anyway. Kudos to Douglas Sutherland for that contribution!
